page: Amazon Web Services r7a.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

The instance is provisioned with 384 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. Network throughput operates at a baseline of 19 Gbps. There is no bundled local instance storage, requiring persistent workloads to utilize external network-attached block storage. The system includes no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier multi-core Geekbench score of 21,368.0 and a Clang compilation score of 63,432.0, alongside 147,629.91 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 223.43 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 136.22 GB/sec. In-memory data throughput is highlighted by 116.77 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 28,961.58.

With its dense DDR5 memory footprint and high parallel processing capabilities, the r7a.12xlarge delivers efficient resource density without the expense of full-socket bare-metal allocations. It is well matched for high-concurrency in-memory databases, large Redis caches, distributed data analytics, enterprise memory-bound ERP systems, and heavy multi-threaded code compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed for high-density transactional and analytical workloads. Built on the AWS Nitro System with x86_64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated physical cores from an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Memory capacity totals 384 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core balance. The instance provides a 19 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no local instance storage. Benchmark tests place the r7a.12xlarge in the upper tier for parallel processing, recording 21,368.0 on Geekbench multi-core, 63,432.0 in Clang software compilation, and 116.77 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. This server configuration is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, extensive caching layers, big data analytics engines, and high-thread compilation tasks requiring substantial memory bandwidth and consistent execution speed without local disk dependencies.
